title: Sort
description: A summer photograph of a level crossing with one wave of it pixel-sorted: the verge is combed into solid horizontal strips, and up the curl the grass is lifted in long sorted rows that climb from the ground and arch over the crossing, each strip ramping from dark green at its root to a bright tail, thinning as it rises; the sheet is lit by its own sort order, dark green where it tucks under the overhang and blooming into white-gold where it turns to the sky, with a few glints breaking off the lit stripe ends, while every pole and sign at the verge stays untouched. Brush anywhere and the picture sorts under your hand, live on the GPU; the longer and harder you brush, the longer the spans grow and the further the rows are stretched up the curl. Press and hold and the sort runs backwards, every pixel sliding home.
intent: After Kim Asendorf's ASDF Pixel Sort (2010, https://github.com/kimasendorf/ASDFPixelSort) and herb's generative reference 2 (a street photo smeared into horizontal strips that curl up like grass). The print's 2400x1600 is cut into bands 8-14 px tall; each is sorted once along its centre row and that row is written down the whole band, so every run is a solid rectangle. Spans may only start on grass and run on, within a reach and an ASDF luminance interval that both grow with the brush, ending once they have run 30% of their reach through anything but vegetation, or at a silhouette in the depth map (Depth Anything V2) or a depth step, so they never cross a pole; sorted by luminance pulled down by greenness, so each run is one ramp from dark green to its brightest pixels, by odd-even transposition in WebGL2 fragment passes; outside a span the same network orders pixels by home index, so erasing the mask sorts every pixel back home. The wave is geometry: the curl is a stack of layers and each layer is one of the verge's own bands, straight along its own row, then bent round the curl's centre and drooping back over the top. So each band's sorted run, rooted where its grass starts right of the crossing's poles, is carried rightward along its own row and only then bends up into the hook: the verge peels into the wave. Every wave pixel is one sorted pixel with hard ends, never a blend: a band rises as two or three sub-strips, each stretching the run by its own amount to its own tail, and as the face recedes a 1-2 px gap of the photo opens between bands; a strip's length follows its run's length, so the lip and the back are combed by the runs. Left of a strip's root the band stays sorted in place, each run slid toward the curl so the photo shows where its pixels left. The curl is lit as a surface by the sort order itself: every strip has a facing along its centre line (its depth through the stack of curl layers and how far that face turns to the sky), and the facing picks the stretch of the run it reads, so the underside and the hook read the dark green heads and stay short while the crest and the upper outer face read out to the warm white-gold tails; glint tiles break off stripe ends only where the facing peaks.

sources.author: XS Xue (@xxs11)
sources.note: 6000x4000 original, shown at 2400x1600; depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py, 1200x800.
